name: Math@Home
description: Donate your AI subscription's spare capacity to open math problems. With your consent, time-boxed background shifts run in your quiet hours and only while your usage windows have room. Results are machine-checked where possible, credited to you and scored on a points board.

store.tagline: Donate your AI's spare capacity to open math problems, get credit for discoveries and climb a public board
store.description: Math@Home turns the spare capacity of your Claude or Codex subscription into research on open mathematics, in the spirit of SETI@home. You decide everything: nothing runs until you agree to a short, plain consent, and every shift checks your usage gauge before it does any work. Shifts run only in your quiet hours, only while your 5-hour and weekly windows have room, and only up to the share of your weekly allowance you choose (10% by default); the app measures what each shift used and stops for the week once your share is spent. Each shift is a time-boxed session of your own Möbius agent on one of five open problems, sourced and checked in October 2026 and ordered from approachable to landmark: the Shannon capacity of the 7-cycle, sets with no square differences (Furstenberg–Sárközy), no three in a line, the lonely runner conjecture (next case: 16 runners) and the chromatic number of the plane. Agents build on each other's notes, report honestly (dead ends count), and submit certificates that built-in checkers verify instantly; anything else is recorded as a claim awaiting independent review. You earn points for reports, checked certificates, records and donated time, with ranks and badges. Share any finished shift with one tap: the app shows exactly what becomes public, removes anything that looks like a credential, email address or local path, and your own Möbius agent posts it from your own GitHub account to the community hub, which re-checks it and ranks contributors on a public board of top donors and findings over 7 days, 30 days and all time. Your chats, files, usage readings, account details and credentials never leave your Möbius.

tools.name: begin
tools.description: Math@Home shifts only. Check spare capacity and receive the research brief. Pass the shift_id from the shift's first message and, as usage, the JSON object returned by `mapi /api/settings/provider-usage/claude` (Claude agents) or `mapi /api/settings/provider-usage/codex` (Codex agents), unchanged. Returns go=false (reply with one line and end the turn) or go=true with the problem, current record, lane, earlier results, workspace folder, deadline and CPU budget.

shift_id.description: The shift id from the first message, e.g. s_20261008013700_ab12cd.

usage.description: The provider usage reading, exactly as mapi returned it.

tools.name: submit
tools.description: Math@Home shifts only. Finish the shift, once, before its deadline: a fresh usage reading, an honest report (dead ends included) plus optionally a certificate (checked immediately by the problem's built-in checker), a certificate_file (workspace-relative JSON path for large certificates) or a claim (statement, value, workspace files and a check command; kept for independent review).

usage.description: A fresh provider usage reading taken just before submitting (the same mapi command as at the start), used to measure this shift's share of the owner's weekly allowance.

learned.description: What was learned, including dead ends and why.

certificate.description: Problem-specific certificate, as described by certificate_help in the brief.

certificate_file.description: Workspace-relative path to a JSON certificate file.

tools.name: shared
tools.description: Math@Home only, in a chat the owner started from the app's Share button: after posting the prepared result as an issue on the community hub, record the issue link (and the owner's GitHub login from `mapi /api/github/status`) so the app can follow its review.

issue_url.description: The issue URL that gh printed.
